primitives.name: Cartesian Product
primitives.verbatim_quote: CARTESIAN PRODUCTS If X and Y are any two sets (not necessarily subsets of the same space), the Cartesian product X × Y is the set of all ordered pairs (x,y), where x ε X and y ε Y.
primitives.assumptions: Sets X and Y are arbitrary and not required to be subsets of the same space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When either X or Y is empty, X × Y becomes the empty set.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's multi-agent state space decomposition; maps to GSI's joint distribution construction via product measures.
layer2.telemetry: Verification via tuple membership in product set.

primitives.name: Rectangle in Product Space
primitives.verbatim_quote: Thus, for instance, if A ⊂ X and B ⊂ Y, we shall call the set E = A × B (a subset of X × Y) a rectangle and we shall refer to the component sets A and B as its sides.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A': 'subset of X', 'B': 'subset of Y', 'E': 'rectangle subset of X × Y'}
primitives.assumptions: A and B are subsets of their respective base sets X and Y.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Empty when either A or B is empty.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE for defining bounded regions in phase space; used in GSI for constructing rectangular event domains in probability space.
layer2.telemetry: Verification via inclusion test of product set elements.

primitives.name: Empty Rectangle Condition
primitives.verbatim_quote: A rectangle is empty if and only if one of its sides is empty.
primitives.assumptions: Rectangles defined as Cartesian products of subsets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When A = ∅ or B = ∅, then A × B = ∅.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's boundary condition detection in state transitions; maps to GSI's null-event handling in probabilistic models.
layer2.telemetry: Boolean check for emptiness of product set.

In GSE, this structure enables modeling of multi-agent system states as tuples across independent dimensions. For GSI, it allows construction of joint probability spaces from marginal distributions. The theorem stating that a rectangle A × B is empty iff one side is empty ensures logical consistency in both systems. This principle underpins conditional independence assumptions in Bayesian networks and provides a formal basis for bounding regions in phase space. The duality between product space and component sets reveals a fundamental symmetry: while individual sets may be simple, their product can encode complex relational structures. Failure modes occur when components are misidentified or when the product space lacks sufficient dimensionality for the modeled phenomena.
